newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Visit of U.N. rights officers to Nigeria postponed.
newsitem.headline: Visit of U.N. rights officers to Nigeria postponed.

text.p: Two United Nations human rights officials due to arrive Nigeria on Sunday for a two-week mission to investigate alleged rights abuses have postponed their visit, their aide said.

Bacre Waly Nidaye, a Senegalese who is the U.N. special rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, and Param Cumaraswamy, a Malaysian who is the U.N. special rapporteur on independence of judges and lawyers, were to stay until March 5.
"The visiting U.N. human rights special rapporteurs will definitely not be arriving today," Alan Parra, an officer at the U.N. Centre for Human Rights in Geneva, told Reuters in Lagos.
"We are seeking certain clarifications on the visit from the Nigerian government. I cannot go into further details," said Parra, in Nigeria since Wednesday preparing for the visit.

Anwalu Yadudu, special adviser to the military government on legal matters, told Reuters by telephone from Abuja that he was unaware of the delay, adding: "We have made ready all arrangements for the visit of the U.N. team."

The U.N. human rights commission watchdog called for the mission after another U.N. mission visiting Nigeria last year called for support for the government's democracy programme but said it found human rights "terrible".

The government of General Sani Abacha turned a pariah in 1995 when it hanged writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight minority rights activists for murder after a trial called flawed by international experts. Another 19 Ogoni youths are in detention facing similar charges.

Many people, including former military ruler Olusegun Obasanjo, his deputy Shehu Musa Yar'Adua and four journalists are behind bars for allegedly plotting to overthrow Abacha, who seized power five months after a previous army ruler annulled a June 1993 poll to restore democracy.
Moshood Abiola, presumed winner of the poll has been held since June 1994 for proclaiming himself president. Dozens of those in opposition to the government are also in detention.
